title: Builder pattern
idea: The Builder pattern collects an object's settings step by step in a separate builder, then creates a valid, immutable object in one final `build()` call.

analogy.text: A sandwich counter: you name the bread, add fillings one at a time, and nothing is handed over until the order is complete.
analogy.breaks: The counter never refuses an order; `build()` rejects invalid combinations.

points: It replaces long constructors where two `int` arguments can be swapped silently.
Required values go in the builder's constructor; optional ones get defaults and fluent setters.
`build()` checks cross-field rules once, so no half-built object ever escapes.

hero.title: From builder calls to one object

messages.label: builder("sync-orders")
messages.note: The required name goes in first. A builder without it cannot exist.

messages.label: this
messages.note: Each setter stores a value and returns the same builder, so calls chain.

messages.label: retries(3).timeoutSec(30)
messages.note: Optional values are named at the call site. Swapping them is now visible.

messages.label: tag("nightly")
messages.note: Collections grow inside the builder. No `JobConfig` exists yet.

messages.label: build()
messages.note: `build()` checks every rule, including ones that span two fields.

messages.label: new JobConfig(this)
messages.note: The private constructor copies the values and freezes the tag list with `List.copyOf`.

messages.label: immutable JobConfig
messages.note: The caller gets a finished object with only `final` fields and no setters.

code.title: The problem: telescoping
code.caption: Overloaded constructors hide argument meaning; setters let an invalid object exist.

walk.text: Each overload adds one parameter and chains to the next. Three optional fields already need four constructors.
Both calls compile: the types match. Only the order of two `int` values tells them apart.
Retries and timeout trade places in the printed line. Nothing warned the author.
The JavaBeans style creates the object first. It is usable before its name is set.
Each setter runs alone, so no rule checks the whole object. A negative timeout slips in.

code.title: The fix: a builder
code.caption: A static nested builder: named steps, defaults, one validation point and an immutable result.

walk.text: The only constructor is private and takes the builder. `List.copyOf` freezes the tags.
The required name is final in the builder. Optional fields start with sensible defaults.
Each setter returns `this`, which makes the fluent chain on lines 7 and 8 work.
`build()` validates single fields and the cross-field worst-case time, then creates the object.
The builder keeps its own list. Adding a tag later cannot change an object already built.
Ten retries of 120 seconds breaks the 600-second rule. The error names the exact problem.

pitfalls: Validating in each setter misses cross-field rules; check the whole object in `build()`.
Passing the builder's own list into the object leaks later changes; copy it in the constructor.
Adding a builder to a two-field class is noise; use a constructor or a `record` there.

quiz.q: Same `JobConfig` as the demo. What does this print?
quiz.why: Setters only store values; rules run in `build()`. By then the timeout is 90, which is valid, and the other fields keep their defaults.

takeaway: Collect settings in a builder; validate once in `build()`; return an immutable object.
